## About

I am a physician from Ghana and currently pursuing my Master of Public Health (MPH) at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.

My journey began in Ghana, where I worked at Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital and Ghana Police Hospital. These experiences grounded me in patient care but also revealed the urgent need for systemic solutions in public health.

Before joining Hopkins, I completed graduate coursework at Emory University, where I took formal courses in SAS and introductory R programming. These courses strengthened my skills in data management and analysis, and sparked my passion for applying quantitative methods to public health challenges.

At Johns Hopkins, I serve as a Graduate Teaching Assistant for Introduction to Public Health and am engaged in research through the Johns Hopkins Surgery Center for Outcomes Research (JSCOR) Surgical Faculty–Student Mentoring Program with Dr. Ahmet Kılıç, focusing on cardiovascular surgery outcomes. Beyond my studies, I co-founded the Vicco61Aid Foundation, established in memory of my late father, to advance community health initiatives in Ghana.

## Research Interests 

Vaccine Epidemiology — Uptake, Equity, Safety, and Effectiveness 

Pharmacoepidemiology & drug safety

Clinical trials 

Surgical and cardiovascular outcomes research
